Due dates and delinquency

Oklahoma ad valorem taxes come due on November 1. The bill turns delinquent on January 1 unless at least half has been paid by then, and 68 O.S. section 2913 allows no more than two installments.

Payment situationOklahoma rule
Bill dueNovember 1
Whole bill delinquentJanuary 1, unless one half or more was paid before that date
Second halfPayable before April 1, then delinquent
Mortgage servicersOne annual payment before January 1
Bills of $25 or lessFull amount before January 1
Interest on delinquent tax1.5 percent per month or major fraction, stopping once interest equals the unpaid tax

Mailed payments count by the date of receipt, since the county treasurer stamps each envelope with its arrival day. If your lender escrows taxes, you probably never see these dates, because the servicer pays in one lump sum.

Who sets the value of an Oklahoma house for tax purposes?

The county assessor sets the value, and the Oklahoma Tax Commission supplies the rules and forms. Under 68 O.S. section 2875, each assessor must follow the Commission's rules and may not use a form the Commission has not approved.

When the assessor raises a house's fair cash value from the prior year, a written notice goes out by mail, marked with the mailing date. Section 2876 requires it to show the current fair cash value, the taxable fair cash value for the preceding and current year, the assessed value and the assessment percentage for both years, plus the taxpayer bill of rights. For a homestead it must also explain the application for a limit on fair cash value under Article X, Section 8C of the state constitution.

Keep that notice with your sale papers. A buyer's title company will see the same numbers on the tax roll.

How to protest a valuation

The assessor must schedule an informal hearing, which can be held in person or by phone if the taxpayer asks. A taxpayer who cannot attend gets at least two more chances, on alternative dates that fall on different days of the week.

Details in section 2876 that are easy to miss:

  • The protest goes on a form prescribed by the Tax Commission and must set out the facts in plain, concise language.
  • The assessor may fix a scrivener's error or other admitted error at any time, even after the 30-day window closes.
  • The decision comes by regular or electronic mail, marked with the mailing date, and that date starts the appeal clock.
  • If the appeal goes to the county board of equalization, the assessor must give the board the taxpayer's submissions, the data supporting the value, and a written explanation of the informal hearing result.

A protest does not pause the bill. Under section 2884, full taxes must be paid when due during an appeal, and a pending appeal is dismissed if the taxes go delinquent. A taxpayer may also protest an unchanged valuation by the first Monday in April (section 2876(F)).

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Oklahoma house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption

Every qualifying homestead gets a $1,000 reduction in assessed valuation, and some owners get a second $1,000. The dollar amounts are small, but they come off assessed value, so claim them while you still live in the house.

  • Base exemption: $1,000 of assessed valuation (68 O.S. section 2889).
  • Additional exemption: another $1,000 for heads of household whose gross household income for the prior year did not exceed $30,000 (section 2890).
  • Value limit: a separate application for the Section 8C limit on fair cash value of a homestead (section 2890.1).

Applications go to the county assessor by March 15, or within 30 days of a valuation increase notice if that is later. A late application generally starts with the following tax year, except for certain tornado cases. Owners 65 or older who previously qualified for the additional exemption need not reapply each year, but must tell the assessor if income rises above the limit.

Estates have a duty here too. An executor or administrator must notify the assessor when a homestead is no longer the homestead of an eligible person. Heirs who keep an inherited vacant house should expect the exemption to end. Our homestead exemption guide covers the rules in more detail.

When taxes go unpaid for years

Once taxes have been unpaid three years or more, the county treasurer must advertise and sell the real estate at the county tax resale. Section 3105 sets the resale for the second Monday of June each year.

A county treasurer may run the resale as an online auction, which can start any time during business hours in the full week of the second Monday of June. Property sells to the highest bidder for cash or certified funds, and the cost of an online auction firm is added to each property's sale. Section 3129 also defines "nuisance property" for parcels with liens above fair market value or environmental problems costing more than the property is worth.

An owner, or anyone with a legal or equitable interest, can redeem before the auction starts. Under section 3113, the payer gives the county treasurer the originally delinquent sum, interest at the lawful rate and any accrued costs. Minors and mentally incapacitated owners have one year after the disability ends, with interest and penalty of no more than ten percent a year.

Counties with more than 100,000 people must skip the sale for some owners. The conditions are a single-family home, an owner of 65 or older (or totally disabled) who owes the tax, no rental use, income at or below the federal guideline level, and a tax roll value of $180,000 or less.

Deed tax when you sell

Oklahoma imposes a documentary stamp tax on deeds for realty sold, at $0.75 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it. It applies when the consideration exceeds $100, measured without counting liens that remain on the property.

Under 68 O.S. section 3202, several deeds are exempt:

  • Deeds between spouses, or between parent and child or close relatives, with no actual consideration.
  • Deeds between a person and that person's own revocable trust.
  • Tax deeds, and deeds of release of property that secures a debt.
  • Foreclosure deeds where the buyer is the mortgage holder.

The tax attaches when the deed is executed and delivered to the buyer. Ask the closing agent to show this line, along with any prorated property tax, on the settlement statement.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Oklahoma houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with back taxes or an open protest

Start by finding out exactly what is owed and which year it belongs to. Call the county treasurer for a payoff figure on delinquent tax; the closing agent then pays it from your sale proceeds.

Section 2885 makes assessor and equalization board proceedings the sole way to correct an assessment or abate taxes, so a value cannot be disputed at closing. When the protest deadline is behind you, the realistic choices are to pay the bill or sell with the valuation as it stands.

Several years of delinquent tax, an inherited house or code violations often block a conventional listing. A cash buyer may purchase such a house as-is, and the title company clears tax liens from proceeds when the numbers allow. Terms depend on the property, and this page is information, not tax or legal advice.

Frequently asked questions

When are property taxes due in Oklahoma?

Property taxes are due November 1. If half or more has been paid before January 1, the rest is due before April 1. Otherwise the whole bill is delinquent on January 1.

What interest does Oklahoma charge on late property tax?

Delinquent taxes bear interest of 1.5 percent per month or major fraction until paid, and interest stops growing once it equals the unpaid principal. A separate five percent monthly penalty applies only to certain nonindividual owners of large property in small-county dependent school districts.

Can I stop a tax sale by paying?

Yes. An owner or anyone with a legal or equitable interest may redeem before the resale auction starts by paying the delinquent sum, lawful interest and accrued costs to the county treasurer.

How much is the Oklahoma homestead exemption?

It is $1,000 of assessed valuation, with another $1,000 for heads of household with prior-year gross household income of $30,000 or less. Apply to the county assessor by March 15.

Is there a deed tax when I sell an Oklahoma house?

Yes. The documentary stamp tax is $0.75 per $500 of consideration when consideration exceeds $100, with exemptions such as certain family transfers without consideration.

title: Oklahoma Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home
content:
Oklahoma Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home

Cash Home Buyers in Oklahoma
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Oklahoma Homestead Exemption: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Oklahoma Homestead Exemption sale
  • Turn the Oklahoma Homestead Exemption offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Oklahoma House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Oklahoma?
We buy Oklahoma houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Two Oklahoma homestead protections

Two separate protections share the name: a property tax exemption under Title 68 and a creditor protection for the home under Title 31. A seller may have one, both or neither, and each is claimed differently.

The tax exemption is a filing with the county assessor that lowers the yearly bill. The Title 31 homestead is not filed anywhere. It is a legal shield that protects a principal residence from forced sale by most creditors, within acreage limits.

What the property tax exemption takes off the bill

It exempts the first $1,000 of assessed value from ad valorem tax. In Oklahoma County that works out to a saving of roughly $87 to $141, so the amount is modest and depends on local millage.

A second $1,000 of assessed value is exempt for a household with gross income from all sources of $30,000 or less. In Oklahoma County that application is renewed each year until the owner reaches age 65.

Oklahoma property tax benefits for homeowners
BenefitMain conditionWhere and when to file
Homestead exemptionOwn and live in the home on January 1; deed on record with the county clerk by February 1County assessor, by March 15
Additional homestead exemptionHousehold income of $30,000 or lessCounty assessor, by March 15
Senior valuation limitationAge 65 or older, head of household, income under the HUD limitCounty assessor, by March 15
Exemption for total disability100 percent service-connected disabilityCounty assessor

Questions on the state application form

Form 921 asks questions that decide eligibility, and a no to the wrong one can end the claim. It wants to know whether any part of the property is rented, whether any is used commercially, whether the owner holds only a partial interest, whether it sits in a trust, and whether the home is a manufactured home.

  • Did you own the property on or before January 1?
  • Did you live in it as your residence on January 1?
  • Will your deed be on record with the county clerk on or before February 1?
  • Do you have, or did you have last year, a homestead exemption elsewhere?

An application filed after March 15, or one with a no in the ownership section, may only count toward the following year.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Oklahoma house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Senior valuation limitation and what happens at sale

The limitation locks the taxable fair cash value of the home for an owner who is 65 or older, is the head of household and has income within the HUD qualifying limit. The limit is $90,300 for the 2026 tax year in Tulsa County, while Oklahoma County's 2025 notice cited $89,500, so the number changes by year.

It does not freeze the tax bill itself. The amount can still rise if the excise board adds millage, a judgment is taken against the county, or voters change assessment percentages.

The limitation ends when title is transferred. A buyer starts fresh, and a seller who is moving does not carry it to the next house automatically.

Applying again after buying a homestead

A new owner has to apply again, because any purchaser or new owner must file an application and the seller's exemption does not pass with the deed.

The statute also puts a duty on the seller side. A taxpayer must tell the assessor in writing about a change in use, and recording a deed or other instrument showing a change of ownership counts as sufficient notice. Owners who keep an exemption they no longer qualify for owe twice the unpaid taxes plus interest and penalty, face a lien, and lose the right to a homestead exemption on any Oklahoma property for two years.

What the Title 31 homestead protects

Under 31 O.S. 2, an urban homestead may not exceed one acre and a rural homestead may not exceed 160 acres. In a city, at least 75 percent of the floor area of the improvements must be the principal residence, and if more than 25 percent is used for business the exemption is capped at $5,000.

Temporary renting does not change the homestead character as long as the owner has not acquired another homestead. Section 31-1 also treats a manufactured home as exempt when it is the owner's principal residence, with no acreage figure stated there.

These rules decide what a judgment creditor can reach when a house is sold, and they are why title companies ask who lives in the home.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Oklahoma houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Does a spouse have to sign the deed?

In most cases, yes. Under 16 O.S. 4, a deed, mortgage or contract affecting an exempt homestead, other than a lease of one year or less, must be in writing and signed by both spouses if both are living and neither is divorced or legally separated.

  • An agent may sign for a spouse only if the power of attorney is recorded with the county clerk in the county where the property sits.
  • A deed recorded for ten years with no court challenge on homestead grounds is treated as valid without the spouse's signature.
  • Missing a spouse's signature on a VA-insured purchase does not void it.

Sellers who inherited a house, or who are separated but not divorced, often discover this requirement late in the process.

Free filing and deed fraud protection

Filing the exemption costs nothing, and the Oklahoma County Assessor warns against companies that charge to prepare and file it. That office rejected 190 applications from a title company that used forms not approved by the Oklahoma Tax Commission.

The county clerk also runs a free deed alert service that notifies an owner by text, phone or email when a document is recorded under their name, which helps catch deed tampering. Each county assessor runs its own filing process, so contact the office for the county where the house sits. The March 15 deadline is the same everywhere, but office hours, online portals and field filing days are not.

How the homestead fits into a quick sale

Homestead status touches three parts of a sale: the tax bill that gets prorated at closing, the spouse's signature on the deed, and whether a creditor has any claim on the proceeds. A seller who never filed for the exemption can still sell, but may have paid more tax than needed.

If a sale happens before March 15, the owner who lived there on January 1 can still file the exemption claim, and a late claim only counts toward the next year. Because a new owner starts over, the buyer should file promptly after closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What is the deadline to apply for the Oklahoma homestead exemption?

March 15, or within 30 days after a notice of valuation increase, whichever is later. A later application can still be filed, but it counts from the following tax year.

Do I have to reapply for the homestead exemption every year?

No. An owner who was granted the exemption and still lives in the home does not have to reapply. The additional exemption for households at $30,000 or less is the exception, and in Oklahoma County it is refiled yearly until age 65.

Does the homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. Any purchaser or new owner must file their own application. The senior valuation limitation also ends when title is transferred.

How many acres does an Oklahoma homestead cover?

One acre inside a city or town and 160 acres in a rural area, under 31 O.S. 2. In town, the principal residence must make up at least 75 percent of the improvements to avoid the $5,000 cap.

Can I sell my house without my spouse signing?

Generally not if it is your exempt homestead and your spouse is living and not divorced or separated. Section 16-4 requires both signatures, with narrow exceptions such as a recorded power of attorney. Filing for the exemption itself is free with the county assessor.

title: Oklahoma Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling
content:
Oklahoma Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling

Cash Home Buyers in Oklahoma
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Oklahoma Estate and Inheritance Tax sale
  • Turn the Oklahoma Estate and Inheritance Tax offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Oklahoma House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Oklahoma?
We buy Oklahoma houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Is there an Oklahoma estate tax?

No, if the death was on or after January 1, 2010. Oklahoma repealed its estate tax statutes at 68 O.S. Sections 801 to 803 as of that date, and the state lien statute says no estate tax lien attaches to estate property for those deaths.

An heir holding a house can cross one worry off the list. No Oklahoma estate tax return is due, and no state tax lien needs clearing before a sale. What is left is federal law, the probate court process and the income tax questions that arise when the house sells.

Treat this as general background on Oklahoma rules rather than legal advice. An estate attorney can say how it applies to a specific death.

Title and the estate tax lien

Under 68 O.S. Section 804.1, a house can pass with clear title as far as estate tax is concerned, and nobody has to get a court order to prove it. The statute separates two groups of deaths.

  • Deaths on or after January 1, 2010: no estate tax lien attaches to property passing through the estate, by joint tenancy or otherwise. No order exempting estate tax liability is needed to release the property or make title marketable.
  • Deaths before January 1, 2010: any estate tax lien ends ten years after the date of death, and again no court order is needed to make title marketable.

The section was added in 2010 and amended in 2017. If a long-vacant inherited house has an old chain of title, the title company may ask about a pre-2010 death, so have the date of death ready.

When a federal estate tax return matters

Only for very large estates. A federal return is due only if gross estate, adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption add up to more than that year's filing threshold. The threshold stands at $13,990,000 for 2025 deaths and $15,000,000 for 2026 deaths.

Most Oklahoma family homes are nowhere near those figures. Portability is a separate option: a surviving spouse may claim whatever exemption the decedent left unused, but only by filing a timely estate tax return. A spouse who wants that option should talk to a preparer even when no tax is due.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Oklahoma house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Income tax after selling an inherited house

Often very little. An heir's basis is generally the home's fair market value at the date of death, a rule found in IRS Publication 551, which also lets the estate's personal representative elect an alternate valuation date.

If the house sells for about what it was worth at death, the gain is close to zero. Gain shows up only when the sale price climbs above that starting value, or after the heir fixes up the house, since repairs add to basis. Keep the appraisal, the estate inventory and every repair receipt in one folder.

One exception applies when the person who died received the house as a gift from you or your spouse in the year before death. Your basis is then the earlier adjusted basis. Our Oklahoma capital gains tax guide covers the Oklahoma return side of the sale.

Can a smaller estate skip some probate steps?

Yes, within limits. Under 58 O.S. Section 241, a court can skip some or all regular probate steps when the estate's real and personal property totals no more than $150,000 and the personal representative applies after being appointed.

The statute lays out a shorter path with fixed notice periods. The court must first confirm the estate is under the limit, and it may order an inventory and an appraisal unless it finds one unnecessary.

Timeline for the shorter procedure in 58 O.S. 241
StepRequired timing
Publish notice to creditors and of the hearingWeekly, two weeks in a row
Creditors file claimsWithin 30 days after publication
Mailed notice to interested personsNo later than 10 days ahead of the hearing
Hearing date35 or more days after first publication
Final account and petition for distributionAt least 5 days before the order

Even on this shorter path, the statute leaves intact any lien for estate or transfer tax due. For a house, the court order naming the heirs is what lets a buyer receive a deed, so timing a sale means counting those weeks.

Where probate is filed and published

A probate case is opened in one county, and the statutes are the same statewide. The required notice runs in a general circulation newspaper there, or in a neighboring county's paper when the home county has none. A small county may offer few publication choices. An heir who lives elsewhere should call the court clerk to learn where the case is filed and when the next hearing can be set.

If the house sits in Oklahoma County, our Oklahoma County property tax guide explains the assessor and treasurer dates that run alongside the probate.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Oklahoma houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Property passed outside a will

Oklahoma's Nontestamentary Transfer of Property Act sits at 58 O.S. Sections 1251 and following and took effect on November 1, 2008. If the person who died left paperwork that moves the house outside a will, a lawyer who handles estates can tell you whether the Act applies and whether probate is needed at all before a sale. That answer changes the timeline more than any tax rule does.

Checklist before you sell an inherited house

Start with the date of death and the status of the court case, then line up the tax and title papers.

  • Order certified copies of the death certificate and, once issued, the court order or letters naming who can sign.
  • Order an appraisal or ask the personal representative for the estate inventory, since that value is your basis.
  • Check whether the death came before or after January 1, 2010, for the lien rule.
  • Find the property tax account and the last payment, because the county bills the parcel no matter who owns it.
  • Plan for the documentary stamp tax (68 O.S. Section 3201) of 75 cents per $500 of consideration, due as the deed is delivered.
  • Have a title company price out any mortgage or lien payoff before you pick a closing date.

If the home needs repairs or has been vacant, selling as-is for cash can cut down the work, and any offer is written for the specific property. A cash buyer is not waiting on a lender, which helps when the court order was only just issued. Even so, the title company handling the closing will ask for the order or letters first, so keep copies handy.

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Oklahoma estate tax in 2026?

No. The state estate tax statutes at 68 O.S. Sections 801 to 803 were repealed effective January 1, 2010, and no estate tax lien attaches for later deaths.

Does a federal estate tax return apply to my parent's house?

Only when the whole estate exceeds the federal threshold, now $15,000,000 for 2026 deaths and $13,990,000 for 2025 deaths.

Do I need a court order to show the title is free of estate tax?

No. Under 68 O.S. Section 804.1, no order is required to release the property or make title marketable for deaths after 2009, and ten years after death ends any older lien.

What value do I use when I sell an inherited house?

Usually market value on the day of death, unless the personal representative picked an alternate valuation date.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has authority to sign, and the court order or letters show that. Check with the probate attorney or title company before you list or take an offer. On the small estate path, the hearing falls at least 35 days after first notice, so budget more than five weeks.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

We buy Oklahoma houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

How an Oklahoma eviction works

Oklahoma evictions run through a court case named Forcible Entry and Detainer, shortened to FED. No one but a judge can order a tenant to leave. Changing the locks, or cutting water, heat, electricity or gas, is off limits to the landlord even if the tenant owes rent.

Small claims court hears most residential cases. The landlord typically asks for possession of the house, a money judgment for unpaid rent and damage, or both.

Selling a rented house does not stop or replace the case. Its pace comes from the tenant's notice dates and the court calendar. Your closing date has no say.

Which written notice comes first

Each reason for removal has its own clock under Title 41. Landlords often lose ground right here, by filing in court without the matching notice.

Written notice by eviction reason
SituationNotice or time period
Rent not paidFive days from written demand, which also serves as the demand for possession (41 O.S. 131(B))
Breach the tenant can fixWritten notice giving 10 days to fix it, with the tenancy ending 15 days after receipt if not fixed (41 O.S. 132(B))
Month-to-month or at-will tenancyWritten notice of 30 days, from landlord or tenant (41 O.S. 111)
Tenancy shorter than month-to-monthWritten notice of 7 days (41 O.S. 111)
Fire, flood or similar emergency caused by tenant24 to 48 hours written notice
Drug-related or threatening crime24 hour written notice

When a lease has a set end date, it lapses on that date by itself unless the parties agreed otherwise.

Delivering the notice

Handing the paper to the tenant is the preferred method when the tenant can be found. Section 111 gives two fallbacks: delivery to a family member over twelve who lives with the tenant, and then posting on the door plus a mailed copy.

  • First choice: personal delivery to the tenant.
  • Second: a family member over age twelve living there.
  • Third: a copy posted in a visible spot on the home, with another copy mailed by certified mail or the Postal Service accountable mail book.

In plain terms there are two routes, post it and mail it, or hand it over through the landlord, a process server or the sheriff.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Oklahoma house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How quickly the case moves once filed

Very quickly. The summons under 12 O.S. 1148.4 puts the trial 5 to 10 days out from issuance and must spell out the claim plus the sum the landlord will take if the tenant stays away.

Section 1148.5 of Title 12 requires service no later than three days before trial. If reasonable efforts at hand delivery fail, the statute allows leaving a copy with a resident over fifteen at the home, or sending certified mail postmarked at least three days before trial.

A tenant who does not show up may lose by default, meaning the landlord wins without argument.

When the judge sides with the landlord

With a possession judgment in hand, the landlord requests a writ of execution from the court clerk, and the sheriff or another officer enforces it. Under 12 O.S. 1148.10 the writ directs removal of the defendant, return of possession to the plaintiff and collection of rent, fees and costs.

  • Any motion for new trial is due in three days, and it leaves the writ in force.
  • Under 12 O.S. 1148.10A the officer or landlord warns the tenant of a return in 48 hours, either in person or by a posted notice.
  • Refusing to leave once the writ is served is a trespass offense carrying a fine of up to $500, up to 30 days in county jail, or both.
  • To appeal, the tenant may post a supersedeas bond within 2 days of judgment, which a judge can extend to no more than 7 days, and must keep paying current rent into the court clerk's office.

Missing a rent payment during an appeal is treated as giving up the appeal.

Locking a tenant out

Wrongfully removing or shutting out a tenant is costly. Section 123 of Title 41 lets the tenant retake possession or cancel the rental agreement, and in both cases collect the larger of twice the average monthly rent or twice actual damages.

If the tenant ends the rental, the landlord must also return recoverable deposits and prepaid rent. A seller who locks a tenant out to clear the house for a buyer ends up with a larger problem than the one being solved.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Oklahoma houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Belongings the tenant leaves behind

Section 130 of Title 41 covers both abandonment and lawful removal after an eviction. Items the landlord judges to have no apparent value may be disposed of, with no duty to account for them.

Items that do appear valuable require a written notice by certified mail to the tenant's last known address. Property left with the landlord for 30 days or longer is conclusively treated as abandoned. The landlord must store items safely and use reasonable care, and may charge storage costs.

When a tenant who was the only occupant dies, 41 O.S. 130.1 sets a separate process for a designated contact, including a 30 day mailed request before property is discarded.

Selling a rented house

Selling does not terminate the tenancy. Section 119 of Title 41 makes the landlord's conveyance valid with no need for the tenant to agree, and rent paid to the seller before written notice of the sale reaches the tenant counts as properly paid.

After written notice, rent goes to the buyer. The seller is freed from duties for anything after that point, and the successor steps into the obligations of the rental agreement.

Showings are permitted within limits. Section 128 lets a landlord bring prospective buyers in with a day's notice, at reasonable times, unless an emergency exists.

What rental owners commonly run into

A case is filed where the house sits, so you will deal with that county's clerk and calendar. Typical snags:

  • A month-to-month tenant is owed a full 30 days of written notice, which may run longer than a buyer's closing window.
  • A tenant who is behind can remain through hearing and appeal by paying rent into court.
  • Property left behind after a hearing means more time and storage duties.
  • A damaged rental can raise habitability disputes before any eviction starts.

Some owners skip all this by selling as is with the tenant in place, so the buyer takes over the lease and whatever is on the court calendar.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

How many days does an Oklahoma landlord have to give for unpaid rent?

Five days from the written demand. When the tenant has not paid by then, 41 O.S. 131(B) lets the landlord terminate the agreement, and the same demand counts as the demand for possession.

Can a landlord evict a tenant without going to court?

No. A judge alone can order a tenant out. A tenant locked out illegally can claim up to twice the monthly rent or twice actual damages under 41 O.S. 123, whichever is higher.

How long does an Oklahoma eviction case take, and can the tenant appeal?

Trial lands 5 to 10 days after the summons issues (12 O.S. 1148.4). A tenant can appeal by posting a supersedeas bond within 2 days, extendable to no more than 7, and must keep paying current rent into court.

Does selling a rented house in Oklahoma cancel the lease?

No. The sale stands without the tenant's consent (41 O.S. 119). The buyer inherits the landlord's duties, and once the tenant is told in writing, rent goes to the buyer.

Can a landlord show a rented house to buyers?

Yes, if the landlord gives a day's notice and comes at a reasonable hour, except in an emergency. Section 128 says the tenant cannot unreasonably refuse entry for showings.

Oklahoma Transfer on Death Deed: How It Works

Cash Home Buyers in Oklahoma
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Oklahoma Transfer on Death Deed sale
  • Turn the Oklahoma Transfer on Death Deed offer down and you owe us nothing

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Oklahoma?
We buy Oklahoma houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

The law behind an Oklahoma TOD deed

The Nontestamentary Transfer of Property Act, at 58 O.S. sections 1251 through 1258, governs these deeds. The Legislature added it in 2008, and it lets an owner name who receives real estate at death without a probate case for that property.

The Act defines "interest in real estate" broadly. Section 1252 covers any estate or interest in, over or under land, including the surface, minerals, structures and fixtures. A house, the lot under it and any mineral rights the owner holds can all go on one deed.

Section 1258 adds that a properly made TOD deed is not a testamentary disposition and cannot be thrown out for failing the formalities of Title 58 or Title 84. It does not have to meet the rules for a will.

What a valid Oklahoma TOD deed must contain

The record owner must sign it, acknowledge it and record it with the county clerk where the land lies before the owner dies. Section 1253 gives a model form that the deed must follow in substance.

  • A statement that the owner has competent mind and legal capacity.
  • The beneficiary's name and a description of the property.
  • Capitalized language saying the deed is revocable and transfers no ownership until death.
  • Two witnesses, whose declarations appear in the notary's certificate along with the owner's.
  • A notary's signature and seal.

The form may use the abbreviation "TOD" in place of the full words. No payment is needed to support the deed, so a recorded TOD deed can name a child, a friend or a charity without any sale price attached. Record it at the county clerk's office in the county of the property, not at the court.

Control during the owner's lifetime

The owner keeps full control. Under section 1257, the owner remains the legal and equitable owner until death and counts as an absolute owner as regards creditors and purchasers.

Three things follow for a seller. Nobody named on the deed has to sign, consent or even be told while the owner lives (section 1252). The owner may sell, mortgage or lease the property as usual. And a recorded deed can be revoked or replaced without the beneficiary's involvement.

A TOD deed therefore does not block a sale. If the owner sells before death, the beneficiary receives nothing, because the property is no longer in the owner's name at death.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Oklahoma house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Changing or cancelling a TOD deed

The owner can revoke it by recording a revocation, or replace it by recording a new TOD deed. Section 1254 requires the instrument to be executed, acknowledged and recorded in the county where the real estate is, and the beneficiary need not sign or be notified.

A later TOD deed cancels all earlier beneficiary designations for the same interest. One point catches families off guard: a will cannot revoke a recorded TOD deed. An owner who wrote a new will leaving the house to someone else, but never recorded a revocation, has not changed who gets the house.

This causes frequent disputes after a death, since the will names one person and the recorded deed names another. The recorded deed wins.

What the beneficiary must do after the owner dies

The beneficiary must record an affidavit with the county clerk within nine months of the owner's death. For an owner who died on or after November 1, 2011, missing that deadline sends the interest back to the owner's estate, which then needs probate.

Affidavit requirementDetail under section 1252
Who signsEach accepting beneficiary, only for himself, herself or an entity he or she has authority over
ContentsVerification of the owner's death, whether the two were married at death, and the legal description
AttachmentA copy of the owner's death certificate
Where to recordCounty clerk of the county where the real estate is
DeadlineNine months from death (deaths on or after Nov. 1, 2011)
NotaryA notarized affidavit is recorded without a separate acknowledgment

A beneficiary may not accept for another named beneficiary. With several beneficiaries, each must handle his or her own share of the acceptance.

Debts and claims that follow the property

Beneficiaries take the property subject to whatever the owner had already recorded against it. Section 1255 lists recorded conveyances, contracts, mortgages, liens, security pledges, executory contracts of sale, options, leases, easements and any interest less than the owner's full interest.

The same section protects beneficiaries in two ways. A spouse the owner married after signing the TOD deed cannot claim against it under 84 O.S. section 44. And a nonconsensual lien against the beneficiary does not attach to the property until the beneficiary's affidavit is recorded.

Medicaid recovery is a separate concern. Under the state's recovery rule, a lien filed against a nursing-home member's real property stays on the property even after it passes by inheritance or will, until the lien is paid or another listed event occurs. Exceptions exist for a surviving spouse, certain children and some siblings living in the home. If a parent received long-term care, ask the Oklahoma Health Care Authority or an attorney how this applies.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Oklahoma houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If a beneficiary dies first, or the owner holds title with someone else

If a beneficiary dies before the owner, that beneficiary's transfer lapses, and the property becomes part of the estate and needs probate.

If the deed names beneficiaries as joint tenants with survivorship, a beneficiary who died first does not undo the joint tenancy among those still living.

Joint owners can use a TOD deed too, but section 1256 vests title in the beneficiary only if the record joint owner is the last of all joint owners to die, and a TOD deed does not sever a joint tenancy. Two spouses who both name the same child therefore pass nothing until the survivor dies.

Selling an inherited house that passed by TOD deed

A beneficiary can generally sell only after the affidavit and death certificate are recorded, because that filing shows in the county clerk's file that title has moved. A buyer or title company will usually want to see it.

Beneficiaries who inherit a house they do not want to keep face the same questions as other heirs: repairs, taxes and utilities, and shared ownership among siblings. Because the property did not pass through probate, no court order authorizes a sale, so every named beneficiary has to sign the deed to a buyer.

A cash buyer may purchase the house as-is once the affidavit is recorded. Whether a TOD deed fits a particular family depends on mortgages, Medicaid planning and the other estate assets, so this page is information rather than legal advice. An Oklahoma estate attorney can review a specific deed.

What to bring to the closing table

A title company handling a TOD inheritance will ask for a short stack of papers. Gather the recorded TOD deed, the recorded beneficiary affidavit with its copy of the death certificate, and the legal description of the property. If there are several beneficiaries, line up each person's signature early, since all of them must sign the deed to the buyer.

Check recorded mortgages, liens and any nursing-home recovery lien before setting a closing date, because those follow the house and are paid from the proceeds.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Does a TOD deed avoid probate in Oklahoma?

For that property, yes, if the beneficiary records the required affidavit and death certificate within nine months of the owner's death. Otherwise the interest reverts to the owner's estate and needs probate.

Can I sell my house if I signed a TOD deed?

Yes. The owner remains the absolute owner as regards purchasers and creditors during life, and the beneficiary's consent is not needed.

Can my will cancel a TOD deed?

No. Under 58 O.S. section 1254, a will cannot revoke a recorded TOD deed. Revocation requires a recorded instrument or a later recorded TOD deed.

Where is a TOD deed recorded in Oklahoma?

With the county clerk in the county where the real estate is located, before the owner dies.

Does the beneficiary take the house free of the mortgage?

No. Beneficiaries take subject to recorded mortgages, liens and other recorded interests the owner had created.

content:
Oklahoma Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House

Cash Home Buyers in Oklahoma
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Oklahoma Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Oklahoma Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House sale
  • Turn the Oklahoma Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Oklahoma House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Oklahoma?
We buy Oklahoma houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Oklahoma and the profit from your house

Oklahoma has no stand-alone capital gains tax. Your profit simply flows into federal adjusted gross income and gets taxed through the Oklahoma income tax return. Long-held Oklahoma land and buildings can qualify for a deduction that shrinks it.

Federal law gets the first say, since it fixes what part of the gain is taxable anywhere. A long-time owner-occupant may owe nothing at either level. A landlord who sells after a short stretch of renting often sees the reverse.

Work through it in this sequence: federal exclusion, Oklahoma deduction, and last the modest transfer tax stamped on the deed. Bring your closing statement and purchase records to a tax preparer for an answer that fits your situation.

Oklahoma deduction for gain on real property

Gain drops out of Oklahoma taxable income when it comes from Oklahoma real estate you held without a break for five years or longer before closing. The Oklahoma Tax Commission's Form 561 handles the claim and cites 68 O.S. Section 2358 and Rule 710:50-15-48.

Attach Form 561 to your resident return, Form 511. The line 10 result moves to Schedule 511-A, line 12. Before listing, note these points from the 2025 form:

  • Enter the sale under property type code 3, with the Oklahoma address, acquisition date, sale date, price and basis.
  • The deduction is capped at the Oklahoma net capital gain that sits inside your federal adjusted gross income.
  • When federal paperwork shows "INHERITED" for the acquisition date, the state form wants the true date.
  • An installment sale qualifies if the holding period was satisfied at the time of sale. Attach a copy of federal Form 6252.
  • Any capital loss carryover from qualifying property lowers the current year's qualifying gain.

"Uninterrupted" means what it says. Four years and ten months falls short, so count from the day title was yours.

Federal home sale exclusion

On your main home, the first $250,000 of gain can be excluded, or $500,000 for a couple filing jointly. IRS Topic 701 states the rule, and Publication 523 supplies the worksheets.

Both tests must be passed during the five years that end on the sale date: two years of ownership and two years of residence, counted as 24 months each. The months do not need to line up. Joint filers need only one spouse to pass the ownership test, though each spouse must pass the use test.

  • A second exclusion is generally unavailable if you excluded gain on a different house in the prior two years.
  • If you are sent a Form 1099-S, report the sale on your return regardless of how much gain is excluded.
  • Gain that exceeds the exclusion is reported on Schedule D and Form 8949.
  • Service members, Foreign Service staff and intelligence community employees posted away on qualified extended duty can elect to freeze the five-year window for up to 10 years.

Excluded gain never enters federal adjusted gross income, so Oklahoma has nothing to tax on that part. The state deduction only helps with what remains.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Oklahoma house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Federal tax rates on the part that is not excluded

Profit on a house kept beyond one year counts as long-term. IRS Topic 409 puts most long-term gain at 15 percent or less for the majority of individuals, with brackets of 0, 15 and 20 percent set by taxable income.

In tax year 2025, single filers paid 0 percent up to $48,350 of taxable income and 15 percent from there up to $533,400. For married couples filing jointly the 0 percent bracket reached $96,700. The brackets are adjusted annually, so pull the current IRS table for your sale year.

Two further rules affect sellers. Selling within a year gives short-term gain, taxed like wages. Depreciation claimed on a rental creates unrecaptured section 1250 gain, capped at a 25 percent rate. Larger investors may also face the net investment income tax covered in Topic 559.

Selling an inherited house

Heirs usually start with a basis equal to the house's fair market value at the date of death. That often wipes out most of the taxable gain. Publication 551 sets this out and lets the estate's personal representative choose an alternate valuation date.

The exception involves gifts: if you or your spouse transferred the property to the decedent in the last twelve months before death, the decedent's adjusted basis applies and market value does not.

Oklahoma helps on the title side. Under 68 O.S. Section 804.1, deaths on or after January 1, 2010 leave no estate tax lien on the property, and the title becomes marketable without a court order. Our Oklahoma estate and inheritance tax guide goes deeper. File the date-of-death appraisal or estate inventory with your closing papers, because a preparer will start there.

Documentary stamp tax on the deed

The deed carries a documentary stamp tax of 75 cents per $500 of consideration, and a partial $500 is rounded up (68 O.S. Section 3201). The tax kicks in once consideration tops $100, leaving out any lien or encumbrance that remains on the property.

Liability arises at the moment the buyer receives the signed deed. Think of it as a fee for transferring title. Income tax on your gain is a different matter, and your holding period does not move the stamp amount.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Oklahoma houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Quick reference table

Oklahoma and federal home sale tax rules
TopicRule that applies
Oklahoma deduction, minimum ownership of real property5 years without a break
Oklahoma deduction paperworkForm 561 with Form 511
Federal exclusion, single filerGain up to $250,000
Federal exclusion, joint returnGain up to $500,000
Ownership and use tests24 months each inside the last 5 years
Basis of inherited propertyUsually market value on the date the owner died
Deed documentary stamp$0.75 per $500 of consideration

Rental properties and landlords

Because the use test is tied to a main home, a landlord often cannot claim the home exclusion. A house you lived in for two of the last five years and rented the rest of the time may qualify in part, and Publication 523 explains how to split it.

Depreciation taken, or allowable, on a rental returns as unrecaptured section 1250 gain at up to 25 percent. The Oklahoma five-year deduction may still apply to Oklahoma real property gain once the holding period is met, because the state rule measures how long you owned the property and ignores who lived there.

If a tenant stands between you and a quick exit, see our Oklahoma eviction notice page. A dispute that drags out the closing can push the sale into a later tax year.

Records to collect before you sell

Gather the paperwork below before you say yes to an offer. It drives the amount of the gain and the year it is taxed.

  • Your purchase settlement statement with price and closing costs.
  • Receipts for work that adds to basis, such as a roof, an addition or a kitchen remodel.
  • Title date, plus the dates you moved in and out, for the ownership and use tests.
  • For an inherited home, the appraisal or estate inventory showing value at death.
  • Past depreciation schedules if the property was ever rented.
  • The planned closing date, because the sale lands in the tax year it closes.

Paying cash changes none of this. Gain equals the amount realized less adjusted basis. A fast, clean closing just lets you see your numbers sooner.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Does Oklahoma tax capital gains on a house sale?

There is no separate capital gains tax. The profit is taxed as income on Form 511, and Form 561 can deduct gain from Oklahoma real property owned for five uninterrupted years or more.

How long do I need to own the house for the Oklahoma deduction?

Five uninterrupted years before the sale. Form 561 and 68 O.S. Section 2358 set that holding period.

Will I owe tax if I sell my primary residence at a profit?

Maybe not. A single seller can exclude up to $250,000 of gain and joint filers up to $500,000. You need to have owned and lived in the home for two of the last five years, 24 months each. Only gain above the limit is taxable.

Does Oklahoma charge a transfer tax on the deed?

Yes. 68 O.S. Section 3201 imposes a documentary stamp tax of 75 cents per $500 of consideration. It applies when consideration is over $100, not counting liens that stay on the property.

What counts as my gain on an inherited house?

Generally the sale price less the fair market value at the date of death, so a quick sale after inheriting often leaves little gain. Keep the appraisal or inventory. A cash buyer does not alter the calculation.

title: Oklahoma Sheriff Sales: Foreclosure Sale Steps and Redemption
content:
Oklahoma Sheriff Sales: Foreclosure Sale Steps and Redemption

Cash Home Buyers in Oklahoma
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Oklahoma Sheriff Sales sale
  • Turn the Oklahoma Sheriff Sales offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Oklahoma House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Oklahoma?
We buy Oklahoma houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What an Oklahoma sheriff sale is and who runs it

An Oklahoma sheriff sale is a public auction of real estate ordered by a court, and the county sheriff conducts it. Most home sales of this kind follow a mortgage foreclosure judgment, though a sheriff can also sell land to satisfy other money judgments.

Foreclosures here are mostly judicial. 12 O.S. section 686 allows real estate pledged as security to be sold only under a court judgment ordering the sale. When one mortgage covers land in two or more counties, the sheriff of each county sells the land in his or her own county.

The judgment also taxes costs, attorney fees and expenses and apportions them among the parties with liens. That is why the payoff by sale time is usually much larger than the missed payments alone.

How a sale is advertised and held

Notice goes out by mail and by publication before the sale. Under 12 O.S. section 764, the party who requested the sale must mail the sheriff's notice by first-class mail at least ten days before the sale to the judgment debtor and to every record lienholder whose interest the sale would wipe out, and must publish it for two successive weeks.

  • The mailed notice carries the legal description, date, time and place, and for an online sale, the internet address and bidding window.
  • If the county has no newspaper, notice also goes on the courthouse door and in five other public places.
  • In counties with 110,000 or more people, the ad runs in a newspaper in the city or township where the property lies.
  • An affidavit proving mailing and publication must be filed in the case.

If a bidder other than the foreclosing party fails to post the required ten percent within 24 hours, excluding Sundays and legal holidays, the sheriff may accept the next highest bid. A sale that skipped the statutory steps can be set aside on the court's motion.

How an Oklahoma County sale works

Oklahoma County runs its foreclosure sales online with Bid4Assets, on the second Tuesday of each month. The Oklahoma County Sheriff's page carries the rules a buyer must meet.

Buyer requirementOklahoma County rule
Sale formatVirtual auction, 10 a.m. Central, second Tuesday monthly
Minimum bidAt least two thirds of the appraised price
Down payment10 percent of the price within 24 hours
BalanceThe remaining 90 percent before the confirmation hearing
Payment formCertified funds payable to the Oklahoma County Court Clerk
Published listTwo consecutive weeks, at least 30 days before the sale

Bidders without internet access can request an offline paper bid packet from Bid4Assets. Properties sell as is, buyers must research liens, easements and encumbrances themselves, and bidders must be at least 18. Other counties may run things differently, since the statute leaves it to each sheriff whether to use an online marketplace.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Oklahoma house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens after the bidding ends?

The sale is not final until the court confirms it. Under 12 O.S. section 765, notice of the confirmation hearing must go by first-class mail at least ten days before the hearing to the same people who got the sale notice and to the high bidder.

Anyone who objects must file a written objection and mail a copy to those same parties before the hearing. The judge may continue the hearing so both sides can support or oppose the objection. If the court finds the sale followed the statute, it enters that finding on the journal and orders the officer to give the buyer a deed.

Meanwhile the purchase money sits with the court clerk until the judge has examined the proceedings, and then the clerk pays the person entitled to it. The statute also bars any buyer's premium on a sheriff sale. Once confirmed, the sheriff's deed conveys what the debtor could have conveyed and must be executed, acknowledged and recorded.

Counties generally record the deed within three weeks to three months of the sale, depending on local terms.

How long a homeowner can stay and what can stop the sale

A homeowner can generally stay until the court confirms the sale. Once the judgment is filed, the sheriff's sale is set for at least 30 days later, and confirmation comes at least ten days after the sale. Practice shifts over time, so confirm current timing with a lawyer.

Ways to avoid losing the home include:

  • Sell the house and pay off the loan, or ask the lender to approve a short sale if an offer falls short.
  • Pay a lump sum the lender's attorney will accept to reinstate, covering missed payments, taxes, insurance, court costs and attorney fees.
  • Offer a deed in lieu of foreclosure, which can bar collection of a deficiency.
  • Apply for a loan modification, which costs nothing to request.
  • File Chapter 13 bankruptcy, which can be filed until confirmation of the sale and requires regular income.

Legal Aid Services of Oklahoma may help eligible people with modification applications and Chapter 13 representation; its foreclosure guide walks through these options.

Can the lender collect more after the house sells for too little?

Only through a strict motion process. The lender must move for a post-judgment deficiency order with the motion to confirm or within 90 days of the sale, and the court then decides the fair market value of the property as of the sale date.

The deficiency order equals the debt with interest, plus costs and the amount owed on prior liens, less whichever is higher: the court's market value or the sale price. If no motion is filed, the sale proceeds count as full payment of the mortgage debt. For an owner facing a big gap between the loan and the house's value, that protection is a reason to attend the confirmation hearing or send a lawyer.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Oklahoma houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Sheriff sales versus tax resales and deed tax

A foreclosure sheriff sale and a county tax resale are different proceedings. Tax resales are run by the county treasurer on the second Monday of June for property with taxes unpaid three years or more, while a sheriff sale follows a court judgment on a mortgage or other debt.

Deed tax has its own rule. Under 68 O.S. section 3202, the documentary stamp tax does not apply to a foreclosure deed given to the mortgage holder who foreclosed. In other foreclosure actions the tax applies and the purchaser pays it, at $0.75 per $500 of consideration under section 3201.

Steps to take before a sale is scheduled

The window to act is widest before the judgment. After judgment a sale date follows quickly, and costs keep adding to the payoff.

An owner with equity may be able to sell traditionally. An owner with a house that needs repairs, carries liens or faces a tight deadline may look at a cash sale, where the buyer purchases as-is and closes through a title company that pays the lender from proceeds. Whether any route works depends on the loan balance, the court deadlines and the property's condition. This page is general information and not legal advice, so talk to an Oklahoma attorney or Legal Aid before deciding.

Frequently asked questions

Is an Oklahoma sheriff sale final when the gavel falls?

No. The court must hold a confirmation hearing, with at least ten days' mailed notice, and approve the sale before the sheriff's deed issues.

How much do I need to bid at an Oklahoma sheriff sale?

The bid cannot be below two thirds of the appraised value. In Oklahoma County, ten percent is due within 24 hours and the remaining 90 percent before the confirmation hearing, paid in certified funds to the court clerk.

Can I stay in my house until the sheriff sale?

Generally yes. The homeowner may remain until confirmation of the sale, which occurs at least ten days after the sale.

Will I still owe money if the house sells for less than the loan?

Possibly. The lender must file a deficiency motion within 90 days of the sale, and if it does not, the sale proceeds count as full satisfaction of the mortgage debt.

Does the buyer at a sheriff sale pay a buyer's premium?

No. 12 O.S. section 765 bars any buyer's premium on a sale.

What probate does when the owner of an Oklahoma house has died

Probate is the court process that proves a will, names someone to act for the estate, pays valid debts and moves title to the people entitled to the property. When the house sat in the decedent's sole name with no beneficiary designation, it usually has to pass through probate before anyone can hand a buyer a clean deed.

The rules sit in Title 58 of the state statutes. There are three main routes: regular administration, summary administration and an ancillary proceeding for people who owned Oklahoma property but lived elsewhere. On any route, an heir cannot convey the house without authority, and that authority comes from the court as letters.

There is no statute of limitation for filing a probate in Oklahoma. A house can sit in a dead owner's name for years, but property tax, insurance and repair problems keep piling up while nobody can sign a deed.

Which court and which county

The district court of the proper county handles the case. Under 58 O.S. section 5, a person who died as an Oklahoma resident is probated in the county where they lived at death, wherever they actually died.

For someone who lived elsewhere, the statute looks first to the county where the person died leaving an estate, then to any county holding part of it. With an out-of-state owner, that usually means the county where the house sits.

Two practical points follow:

  • Whoever holds the original will must deliver it to the district court or the named executor within thirty days of learning of the death (58 O.S. section 21).
  • An executor or administrator who lives outside Oklahoma may serve, but must first appoint an agent who lives in the county of the case (58 O.S. section 162).

Timeline from petition to final decree

A case moves through a petition, a hearing, letters, an inventory, creditor notice, any sale, a final account and a decree. The fixed pieces in Title 58 look like this.

StepTiming under Oklahoma law
Hearing on a petition to admit a willSet 10 to 30 days after filing (58 O.S. section 25)
Mailed notice to heirs and deviseesAt least 10 days before the hearing
Oath and lettersOath taken before letters issue (58 O.S. section 161)
InventoryWithin two months of appointment, unless the court extends it (58 O.S. section 281)
Notice to creditorsFiled within two months of letters, with a presentment date at least two months out (58 O.S. section 331)
Hearing on final accountAt least 20 days after the petition is filed (58 O.S. section 553)
Real property distributedCertified copy of the final decree recorded with the county clerk

Contested wills, missing heirs and unpaid claims stretch the schedule.

Who runs the estate when there is no will?

The court picks from the priority list in 58 O.S. section 122: the surviving spouse (or someone the spouse requests), the children, the father or mother, brothers and sisters, grandchildren, the next of kin entitled to share, creditors, and finally any legally competent person.

Where several people stand equally, relatives of the whole blood come before half blood, and the court may grant letters to one or more of them. Only the appointed personal representative can sign the estate's deed, so siblings cannot each sell a share of an unprobated house and expect a title company to accept it.

While a case is pending, the court can appoint a special administrator. That person must collect and preserve the estate and take charge of and preserve the real estate from damage, waste and injury (58 O.S. section 215), which helps when the house is vacant and deteriorating.

Creditor claims and the house

Creditor claims set a clock that has to run out before the estate can safely close, and they can force a sale. The personal representative must publish the creditor notice once a week for two consecutive weeks in a county newspaper, with the first publication within ten days of filing, and mail it to known creditors.

Claims not presented by the date in the notice are barred forever. Mortgages are the exception that matters most to house sellers: 58 O.S. section 333 states that nothing in the claims chapter limits the right or time to foreclose a mortgage on a decedent's real property. A lender keeps its remedy even after the claims period closes.

Claim handling follows set rules:

  • The personal representative must allow or reject each claim within 30 days of presentment.
  • A claim not acted on within that window is treated as rejected.
  • A rejected claimant has 45 days from rejection to sue if the claim is due.
  • No suit may be filed on a claim that was never presented to the representative (58 O.S. section 341).

If the house carries a reverse mortgage, a home equity line or unpaid taxes, find those balances early, because they come out of the sale price at closing.

When the estate can sell the house

The estate can sell once the court authorizes it, either by an order of sale or because a will's power of sale has been confirmed. Even when the will grants a power of sale, the court must still confirm the sale unless every heir, devisee and legatee has waived confirmation.

With no power of sale in the will, the representative can petition for permission and attach written consents from all heirs, devisees and legatees. Under 58 O.S. section 239, the court may then authorize the representative to sell and sign deeds without a later return of sale or confirmation. Without unanimous consent, the full procedure in 58 O.S. section 380 and following applies, which includes appraisal, notice by mail and publication, and court confirmation.

If the court orders a public auction instead of a private sale, section 421 requires notice once a week for two weeks in each county where the land lies, plus mail to known heirs, with the sale day no earlier than ten days after first publication.

Estates that can skip regular probate or use a shorter version

Several can. Property held in joint tenancy with survivorship, in a trust, or with a named beneficiary passes outside the probate estate, and smaller estates may use shortened procedures.

  • Joint tenancy: a surviving joint owner records an affidavit of surviving joint tenant and a certified death certificate in the county where the land lies (58 O.S. section 912).
  • Trust: the trustee records a memorandum of trust with the county clerk when conveying trust real estate (60 O.S. section 175.6a).
  • Transfer on death deed: the beneficiary records an affidavit within nine months of the owner's death or the interest returns to the estate.
  • Personal property up to $50,000: heirs can use an affidavit, but that route is for personal property and does not move a house.
  • Estates up to $150,000: under 58 O.S. section 241 the court may dispense with parts of regular proceedings after an inventory, with creditors filing claims within 30 days of publication and a final hearing set at least 35 days after first publication.

If a beneficiary named on a transfer on death deed dies before the owner, the property falls back into the estate and needs probate.

Selling an Oklahoma estate house quickly

Expect a waiting period built from notices, hearings and a vacant property that still costs money. Even a clean case takes months, because creditor notice alone requires a presentment date at least two months after filing.

Common pressure points include:

  • Property tax, insurance and utilities keep running while letters are pending.
  • Heirs who live in different states must each sign consents for a shortened sale.
  • Values listed in the inventory can matter later, since they may be used to set a stepped-up tax basis, so a documented valuation is worth having.

A cash buyer can purchase an estate house as-is once the personal representative holds authority to sign. Bring the letters, the order or consents authorizing the sale, and a death certificate, because a buyer and title company will ask for all three. This page is general information, and an Oklahoma probate attorney should confirm which route fits a particular estate. Free help is available through Legal Aid Services of Oklahoma for those who qualify.

Frequently asked questions

Do I always need probate to sell a house in Oklahoma after someone dies?

No. If the house passed by joint tenancy with survivorship, a trust or a recorded transfer on death deed, title can move without a probate case. If it was in the decedent's sole name with no such designation, probate is normally required before a deed can be signed.

How long does Oklahoma probate take when there is a house?

It varies by estate. The statute sets fixed pieces, such as a hearing 10 to 30 days after a will petition, an inventory within two months and a creditor presentment date at least two months after filing, so even a simple case commonly runs several months.

Can one heir sell an inherited house in Oklahoma on their own?

Not without authority. Only a court-appointed personal representative can convey estate real estate, and if the will has no power of sale the court generally needs the written consents of all heirs, devisees and legatees or must confirm the sale.

What happens to a mortgage on a house in probate?

The mortgage stays attached. Under 58 O.S. section 333, the creditor claims deadline does not limit a lender's right to foreclose, so loan payments should continue or the lender may foreclose on the property.

Is there a deadline to open probate in Oklahoma?

There is no statute of limitation on filing a probate. Delays still create costs, such as ongoing taxes, insurance and possible title problems.
